title: Brazilian Iron Ore: Squeezed Margins, Resilient Shipments
section_path: Brazilian Iron Ore: Squeezed Margins, Resilient Shipments
section_path_text: Brazilian Iron Ore: Squeezed Margins, Resilient Shipments
summary:
Main
Image reference: assets/2026-11-16_brazilian-iron-ore-squeezed-margins-resilient-shipments_img_rgb-color-brs-shipbrokers-monogram-l_c365f35f1de5.png
As November begins, the release of major miners' third-quarter reports points to a dual squeeze on iron ore earnings from weaker CFR prices and higher shipping costs. Vale, for example, reported a 39% y-o-y decline in iron ore fines EBITDA, despite resilient sales volumes. According to Vale's financial report, its average realised iron ore fines price fell from $94.4/t in 3Q25 to $85.1/t in 3Q26., while average freight costs rose 21%, from $18.8/t to $22.8/t.
